display.purpose: Landing headline only, inside the empty drawing area; balanced wrap.

wordmark.purpose: evmdec, lowercase, one word, first header cell; no logo exists.

title.purpose: Report section headings; also the weight of the primary button and scale-line emphasis at body size.

body.purpose: UI text, finding titles and bodies (70ch), landing copy (70ch), report prose (90ch).

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase cell labels, column headings (600) and index group headings; muted ink above a 500-weight tabular value.

severity.purpose: CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW / INFO in a finding row; colour only tints the word.

code.purpose: The drawing, pre blocks and the address field; tab-size 4; function names at 600.

code-small.purpose: Function index rows, evidence wells, finding meta code; report code is 12.5px.

shadows.name: tab-underline
shadows.purpose: The selected tab's 2px rule, drawn inset; the only box-shadow in the system and not an elevation.

borders.name: line
borders.purpose: Heavy rule between regions: header, title block, the three columns, tab strip, outline buttons, error (rubric).

borders.name: hair
borders.purpose: Light rule inside a region: cells, rows, tab dividers, scale line, evidence wells, report tables.

borders.name: revision-cloud
borders.value: border: 6px solid transparent; border-image: var(--cloud) 6 round
borders.purpose: Scalloped outline on a flagged code line; --cloud is an inline 18x18 SVG of eight 3px arcs stroked in the sheet rubric (vermilion in light, amber in dark). Positioned absolutely from calc(12em - 7px) to 4px from the right edge.

focus.name: focus-visible
focus.purpose: Every control; blue in light, amber in dark; no border change or glow.

motion.name: lit-settle
motion.purpose: The only transition: the lit background on code lines and findings, declared under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference only.

breakpoints.name: two-column
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: index 240px, details drop below full width with a top rule, title block 4 per row.

breakpoints.name: stacked
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: frame unfixes, header wraps, title block 2 per row, columns stack (index list 40vh, drawing panel 70vh).

layout.frame: body grid-template-rows: auto auto minmax(0,1fr); 100% height; columns scroll independently

accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on both themes including code highlighting and severity colours
Severity and confidence printed as words; colour never carries severity alone
Minimum 24x24 targets on every button and line link
ARIA tablist with roving tabindex, aria-selected, aria-controls; aria-expanded findings; aria-current index rows; aria-pressed theme toggle
Polite role=status live region announces theme changes and chosen findings
Theme follows prefers-color-scheme with data-theme override persisted to localStorage

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Drawing Set"**

The contract is a built structure and the page is its drawing set. Metadata lives in a title block of eight labelled cells across the top; functions are an indexed sheet list (F-01, F-02, ...) down the left; the decompiled code is the drawing in the middle; every finding is a numbered callout in the code gutter keyed to a detail at the right. The world refuses the category's console (side nav, dark slate, badges) and the report-PDF arrangement. Everything is drawn in line: one-pixel rules divide every region, nothing has a shadow, nothing has a radius except the callout circles, and nothing is labelled twice.

Two sheets exist. In light the page is a whiteprint: a white sheet, iron-black line and type, one vermilion rubric reserved for callouts, the risk figure and the error border. In dark it is a blueprint: Prussian-blue ground, pale line and type, an amber rubric in the same reserved role. The theme follows the system and can be overridden by the header toggle; both sheets meet WCAG 2.2 AA including the code highlighting and the severity colours.

Density is that of a drawing, not a dashboard: 14px body on a 1.45 line, 13px mono code on a 1.5 line, tracked 11px uppercase labels over tabular values, 12px meta. The interface stays out of the way so the code, the findings and the layout are read at reading quality. The only motion is the lit background settling in over 200ms; nothing else moves, and reduced motion removes even that.
keyCharacteristics: Hairline rules at 1px divide every region; no shadows, no fills for structure.
One rubric colour per sheet (vermilion / amber), used only for callouts, the risk figure and errors.
Zero radius everywhere except the 24px circular callout.
Tracked uppercase 11px labels over 500-weight tabular values.
System sans for UI, system mono for code, selectors and evidence; no external fonts or scripts.
Fixed-cell lists whose columns never move; the chosen line or finding stays lit until another is chosen.
A scalloped revision cloud outlines every flagged line of the drawing.

rules.name: The One Rubric Rule
rules.body: Each sheet has exactly one accent and it marks only what a reviewer would mark in red: the callout, the cloud, the risk figure, an error. Nothing decorative, no links, no buttons wear it.

rules.name: The Words First Rule
rules.body: Severity and risk are read from the printed word (HIGH, 76/100 · High); the colour tints the word and never stands alone. A risk score under 8 drops the rubric and prints in ink at weight 500.

rules.name: The Two Sheets Rule
rules.body: Every token has a whiteprint and a blueprint value, and every pair meets AA contrast on its ground. Add a colour to both sheets or to neither.

rules.name: The Tracked Label Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a cell is 11px uppercase tracked 0.08em in muted ink, set above its value, and never repeated as a heading elsewhere.

rules.name: The Ink Code Rule
rules.body: Code is set in ink: keywords, types, numbers and function names share the text colour; only comments drop to muted and strings take green. Emphasis in code is weight (600 function names), not colour.

rules.name: The Fixed Cell Rule
rules.body: Index rows, title-block cells, code lines and finding rows are grids with fixed first columns; content never shifts a column. Long names break at `(` and `,` via soft wraps, long addresses break anywhere, but the grid does not move.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts off the sheet. Hierarchy is drawn with rules, fills and weight; a shadow, a glow or a blur is a foreign material.

dos: Do divide regions with 1px rules: `line` between regions, `hair` within them; a region's boundary is a rule, never a fill or a shadow.
Do set every label at 11px uppercase tracked 0.08em in muted ink above a 500-weight tabular value, and label each thing once.
Do keep the rubric for callouts, the revision cloud, the risk figure at 8 or above, and error borders; the light sheet uses vermilion, the dark sheet amber.
Do print severity and confidence as words beside each other; colour only tints the severity word.
Do give every control at least a 24x24 target and the 2px offset focus outline; use `aria-current`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected` and the polite `role=status` region for every state change.
Do define any new colour on both sheets and verify AA contrast on each ground.
Do use the lit fill (straw / umber) for exactly the chosen item: one index row, one code line, one finding.
donts: Don't add border-radius to anything but the 24px callout circle; buttons, inputs, tabs, wells and notices stay square.
Don't add box-shadows, glows, blurs or gradients; the only inset shadow is the 2px selected-tab underline used as a rule.
Don't load external fonts, icon fonts or scripts; type is the system sans and system mono stacks, and icons are inline SVG at 16px.
Don't colour code tokens beyond ink, muted comments and green strings, or convey emphasis in code with colour instead of weight.
Don't let a column move: fixed first cells (3.4em line numbers, 8.6em callout cell, 3.2em sheet number, 30px finding number) hold their width regardless of content.
Don't animate anything but the lit background (200ms ease-out), and never under reduced motion.
Don't introduce badges, pills, side navigation or a dark-slate console; the dark sheet is Prussian blue, not grey.
